📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

European Union top officials and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham unveiled deals on trade and youth mobility at Friday's Brussels summit.

This might be the first step to rebuild ties, a decade after Britain voted to leave the EU.

During the delegations' meeting, Burnham stated the deal was a "landmark agreement," while European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called it a "turning point" in relations.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, "This is a good day for Britain. This is a good day for Europe," Burnham said.

Speaking at the joint press conference, European Council President Antonio Costa said the bloc respected the British decision to leave the EU and would respect its choice to strengthen ties in the post-Brexit era.

He noted jokingly that the EU and UK "may drive on the opposite sides of the road, but what matters is they are heading for the same direction.".

Industry observers note that burnham said that the deals were made with young people in mind, adding: "This deal is for you. This deal really is about lifting your life chances.".

He went further and stated "Brexit took opportunities from young people," and that they have to "open up new opportunities" for young people.

Von der Leyen said the youth experience project would "open horizons and create friendships that will last a lifetime.".

She mentioned the trade agreement is a "two way street" and it means "more choice for the customers.".

Von der Leyen also mentioned the agreement on the carbon market, saying that it would cut emissions and generate investments in cleaner industries.

She also remarked Britain will rejoin the Erasmus+ program, adding, "We miss them so much.".

Burnham said the agreements reached Friday, however, represent the most the UK could achieve at the moment, "What we are announcing today is probably ‌the limit of what we can achieve in this ‌Parliament, given what needs ‌to be done to implement it.".

In September, Burnham noted he would seek a political consensus on the country's future relationship with the EU, even suggesting he could campaign to take Britain back into the bloc at the next election.

Sources indicate that "Britain and Europe share values, interests and a global neighborhood. In a more dangerous world, we are stronger together. A closer partnership with Europe is good for working people, good for Britain and good for Europe," Burnham mentioned as he arrived in Brussels.

The three key agreements establish ways to:.

The "youth experience scheme" would allow 100,000 people under 30 from each side to reside for up to three years in each other's territory for work, study or travel without being subject to existing visa requirements.

Sources indicate that no deal was reached on tuition fees for EU students studying in Britain, a deal-breaker for the bloc. The EU has pressed for the UK to reduce university tuition fees for EU students to the same level paid by British students.

"There will be further discussions coming out of it on issues including on tuition fees," Burnham said.

Von der Leyen ‌said ⁠she was confident negotiators would reach a ​solution ​on ‌tuition fees, "We will be working ‌on that in ‌the ​next month and as we have a ​track record of finding ⁠solutions,.".

Recent findings suggest that on the food deal, the EU and UK have agreed to scrap certificates and border checks on food and animal products to ease post-Brexit trade. In return, Britain will align more closely with EU food safety and animal health rules.

They also agreed to link their emissions-trading systems, allowing them to recognize each other's carbon allowances and exempt traded goods from carbon border taxes.

According to the AFP news agency, London estimates the deal could boost the British economy by 3.8 billion pounds annually, and spare 6.5 billion pounds worth of steel, aluminum and other industrial exports from additional taxation.

Leaders said they will establish a "structured dialogue on migration." Their joint summit statement said this would include "engagement with third countries" and "returns to third countries," among other issues.

The two sides agreed to launch formal talks on economic security and strengthen cooperation on export controls and supply chains, among other areas.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SpaceX debuted a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast.

Sources indicate that A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m. EST (8:20 p.m. local California time; 0420 GMT on Nov. 21), on a Space Force mission called USSF-317.

The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100.

SpaceX ended its launch webcast just after that touchdown, so we didn't get to see the Falcon 9's upper stage power its way to orbit.

USSF-317 is a classified mission, so we don't know what the upper stage is carrying or where exactly it's headed. However, some experts think that USSF-317 may be hauling a batch of SpaceX's Starshield satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO) for the Space Force's Space Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio, which helps the military keep tabs on potential targets around the world.

NROL-105 | USSF-385 | 8 Starlink missions.

USSF-317 was the 121st Falcon 9 launch of 2026 and the third mission that SpaceX has debuted for the Space Force so far in November.

The vast majority of this year's Falcon 9 missions — about 70% of them — have been devoted to building out SpaceX's Starlink LEO internet constellation, which right now consists of more than 11,000 satellites.

According to recent reports, the Falcon 9 has been putting up incredible numbers lately — it flew a whopping 165 times in 2025, for example — but the workhorse rocket is on its way out. SpaceX plans to retire both it and the Falcon Heavy in favor of its fully reusable Starship megarocket, which deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites on its most recent two test flights.

#82017. Is free will an illusion? Fresh brain research reveals a surprising twist

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (875 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Is free will an illusion? Fresh brain research reveals a surprising twist

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (875 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Imagine you’re in line at your favorite bakery, deciding whether to have a doughnut or a tart.
  • Industry observers note that by the time you’re at the front of the line, however, only tarts are left.
  • These two decisions feel completely different.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Imagine you’re in line at your favorite bakery, deciding whether to have a doughnut or a tart. You weigh them up, the doughnut wins, and you settle on that.

Industry observers note that by the time you’re at the front of the line, however, only tarts are left. So, you buy one.

These two decisions feel completely different. One involves deliberation based on our unique and personal preferences, while the other involves simply recognizing and picking the only available option.

But our latest research published in the journal Imaging Neuroscience shows our brains actually make these decisions in surprisingly similar ways.

When we make free decisions, we recognize multiple options exist, weigh them up, and commit to one based on something internal: our preferences, values and goals.

Industry observers note that forced decisions are different. There’s only one possible outcome, and our job is simply to identify the option and take it.

Because free decisions feel so closely tied to who we are, neuroscientists have long assumed they rely on different processes in the brain compared to forced decisions. Some brain imaging studies support this, showing different patterns of neural activity distributed across the brain.

However, knowing where in the brain free choices happen tells us little about how they are formed – and whether this process is any different from forced decisions.

Decades of research have shown that, to make decisions, our brains gradually gather evidence for each option over time.

In a recent development, think of it like a judge evaluating the facts of a case. Once enough evidence has been accumulated in favour of one party, a verdict is reached. For some types of decisions, this happens very swiftly (over hundreds of milliseconds), making it feel like the choice just popped into your head.

By measuring electrical brain activity, researchers have identified a brain signal that reflects this accumulation of evidence during simple decisions – such as judging whether a traffic light is red or green.

Industry observers note that like a loading bar building to 100%, the signal gradually rises to a particular level before a decision is made. Because the action of neurons in the brain is noisy, this decision-making process also occurs in a noisy fashion: rather than climbing steadily towards one option, the signal fluctuates back and forth between the alternatives.

This partly explains why we aren’t always consistent with our choices – even when our preferences are stable, some days we will go for the tart and others, the doughnut.

Sources indicate that this signal has been identified for forced decisions with a clear correct answer. But what about choices that are open-ended – shaped not just by what’s in front of us, but by something internal like preferences or personal goals?

To answer this question, we recorded people’s brain activity while they chose between sets of colored balloons. They viewed either two balloons of different colors to freely choose between, or a single balloon they were forced to pick.

They pressed a button the moment they made their choice, and we tracked how brain activity unfolded in the lead-up to that moment.

According to recent reports, for both free and forced decisions, the brain activity unfolded in a very similar way. Like a loading bar, it climbed steadily to the same peak level just before a choice was made. When people decided rapidly, the signal increased faster. When they took longer, it rose more slowly.

That’s exactly what you would expect if the brain were tracking and weighing up evidence over time, rather than simply reacting to a decision at the last moment.

From this finding, one might assume the brain forms free and forced decisions in the same way, suggesting decision-making in the brain may be more automatic than it feels.

Industry observers note that this echoes famous experiments by neuroscientist Benjamin Libet in the 1980s. He and colleagues found brain activity begins ramping up before people are even consciously aware of their intention to act – suggesting the brain has already begun deciding before the person consciously realizes they’ve made a choice.

But while the process may be automatic, what the brain is accumulating tells a different story. The evidence it weighs up is drawn entirely from who you are – your preferences, your goals, your experiences. Two people may go through the same neural process and land on the same choice, and yet arrive there for completely different reasons.

So rather than asking whether our choices are truly free, perhaps the better question is what it really means for a choice to be yours. And the next time you find yourself in line at the bakery, know that your brain has already been quietly gathering evidence toward your baked good of choice, and that choice happens a little faster than you realize.

Target on Wednesday reported its best sales growth in more than five years and beat Wall Street's revenue expectations, the latest signs of its turnaround strategy taking hold.

The retailer mentioned its net sales grew 7.1% during the fiscal third quarter. Comparable sales rose 5.6%, compared with StreetAccount estimates of up 3.8%. That growth was boosted by a 5% increase in comparable traffic, Target added.

"[It's] a healthy sign that guests are responding to our changes and choosing Target more often," CEO Michael Fiddelke told reporters.

Digital comparable sales jumped nearly 10% during the quarter.

Recent findings suggest that encouraged by the growth, Target raised its full-year guidance, upping its net sales growth guidance by 1 percentage point to around 6%. It's also expecting full-year operating income margin rate to be around 6.2%, which includes roughly 1.1 percentage points of benefit from tariff refunds.

The manufacturer also noted it's now projecting full-year earnings per share to be in a range of $10.65 to $11.40, compared with prior guidance of between $9.90 and $10.90.

"The changes we've made across our assortment and guest experience are adding up," Fiddelke told reporters. "While we're encouraged by the progress, we know there's more work ahead to sustain this momentum and deliver consistent growth over time.".

Target shares climbed about 7% in afternoon trading Wednesday.

Here's how the company performed in its fiscal third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

Sources indicate that for the quarter ended Oct. 31, Target reported net income of $1.21 billion, or $2.65 per share, up from $689 million, or $1.51 per share, a year earlier.

According to recent reports, this year, the company noted it's invested approximately $3.8 billion in capital expenditures, up nearly $1 billion from last year. Because of those returns, Fiddelke said Target is now expecting to invest between $5 billion and $6 billion in capex next year.

On a call with analysts, he added that those investments will go toward more store remodels, technology, supply chain improvements, among other initiatives.

It has been revealed that the firm noted it saw particular strength in beauty, which saw 9% growth, and food and beverage, where sales increased nearly 7%. The retailer added that net sales rose in all three months of the third quarter, with the strongest performance during the back-to-school season.

Fiddelke told reporters the quarter's strength highlighted "continued progress" toward Target's priorities that it outlined at the beginning of its turnaround.

As it looks to the holiday season, Target noted it's marketing thousands of products priced at $5 and under, along with new artificial intelligence-powered shopping experiences to drive engagement. Fiddelke said Target is "encouraged" by shopping behaviors it's seen so far in the current quarter.

Recent findings suggest that the big-box retailer has been showing signs of returning to growth, as it sees stronger sales trends after years of flat revenue. The results come after Target last quarter hiked its full fiscal-year outlook and noted it saw "broad-based" strength across its various categories.

According to recent reports, it's also lowered prices on more than 10,000 items in an effort to get customers back into its stores, especially as consumer sentiment lags and inflation remains high. The retailer stated on Wednesday that it cut prices on an additional roughly 2,000 items during the third quarter.

Target's stock is up more than 70% this year.

#82013. This 6-million-year-old whale may have had the most crooked face in mammal history

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (999 w)

Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

This 6-million-year-old whale may have had the most crooked face in mammal history

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (999 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A bizarre prehistoric whale that lived roughly 6 million years ago had a face so crooked that researchers initially suspected its fossilized skull had been distorted after death.
  • Sperm whales and pygmy sperm whales are already known for having some of the strangest head shapes among mammals.
  • According to recent reports, now, an international team of scientists has identified an extinct pygmy sperm whale species that took this unusual anatomy to an entirely newly introduced level.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A bizarre prehistoric whale that lived roughly 6 million years ago had a face so crooked that researchers initially suspected its fossilized skull had been distorted after death. Instead, its extraordinary shape was completely natural and may represent the most extreme facial asymmetry ever documented in a mammal.

Sperm whales and pygmy sperm whales are already known for having some of the strangest head shapes among mammals. While most vertebrates have bodies and skulls that are roughly symmetrical on both sides, toothed whales have evolved uneven skull structures to accommodate specialized organs responsible for producing sound and navigating through echolocation.

According to recent reports, now, an international team of scientists has identified an extinct pygmy sperm whale species that took this unusual anatomy to an entirely newly introduced level. Named Scaphokogia huachafo, the whale lived during the Late Miocene, between 6.3 and 5.6 million years ago, and measured approximately 2.7 meters in length. Its fossilized skull displays the most extreme facial asymmetry known in any whale or dolphin, and possibly in any mammal.

A Prehistoric Whale With an Extraordinary Skull.

"Cranial asymmetry in toothed whales is directly linked to the development of fatty structures in the forehead that are involved in sound production. But in Scaphokogia huachafo, this asymmetry went far beyond the area around the blowhole. Both bony nostrils are shifted entirely to the left side of the skull, while the facial bones differ dramatically in size and position. The skull looks completely crooked," explains Aldo Benites-Palomino, lead author of the study.

According to recent reports, benites-Palomino investigated the fossil during his doctoral research at the University of Zurich's Department of Paleontology. He is right now an assistant professor at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (FAU).

According to recent reports, the whale's extraordinary appearance also inspired its scientific name. The word huachafo comes from Peruvian Spanish and is commonly used to describe something excessively flashy, bizarre, extravagant, or even tacky.

"In Peru, huachafo is an everyday word for anything that is flashy, over-the-top, bizarre, extravagant or difficult to categorize aesthetically," says Benites-Palomino.

"When we looked at the proportions of this whale - with its face strongly shifted to the left and its oversized, downward-curving snout - it broke every rule of symmetry and elegance seen in living cetaceans. Its anatomy is so extravagant and odd that huachafo seemed the perfect name for it.".

Scientists Initially Suspected the Skull Was Deformed.

Sources indicate that the remarkable fossil was originally recovered during the mid-1990s from the Pisco Formation in southern Peru. This desert region is famous among paleontologists for its exceptionally preserved fossils of ancient marine animals.

Benites-Palomino first encountered the specimen in 2015 while preparing his Bachelor's thesis at the Museo de Historia Natural in Lima. Its dramatically uneven shape immediately raised an key question: Was the skull genuinely this crooked when the whale was alive, or had millions of years of geological pressure distorted it?

"The initial suspicion with skulls this distorted is always taphonomy - that the specimen may have been flattened or twisted by sediment pressure over millions of years," notes Benites-Palomino.

Recent findings suggest that "But the sutures are fully closed, and there are no fractures, pathologies or deformations elsewhere on the skull. This was genuine biology, not a result of poor preservation.".

The findings confirmed that the extraordinary asymmetry was part of the whale's natural anatomy, rather than damage caused by burial, fossilization, or disease.

A Bizarre Adaptation for Hunting Along the Seafloor.

Sources indicate that the whale's unusual skull also offers clues about how it survived. Modern sperm whales typically pursue squid in deep ocean waters, but Scaphokogia huachafo appears to have followed a very different hunting strategy. Its anatomy suggests that it was highly adapted to searching for food along the bottom of shallow coastal waters.

One of its most distinctive features was a large, tube-shaped snout strengthened by dense bone and cartilage that had hardened into bone. These heavy structures served as natural ballast, moving the whale's center of gravity forward and downward.

Sources indicate that its snout also pointed downward at an angle of 31 degrees relative to the rest of its skull. By reconstructing the joint connecting the skull to the first neck vertebra, known as the atlas, scientists determined that Scaphokogia could bend its head downward by as much as 55 degrees.

"The entire cranio-cervical complex is modified to point the snout directly toward the bottom," explains Gabriel Aguirre-Fernández, co-author of the study and doctoral advisor at the University of Zurich.

"The combination of dense bone, the downward-curving snout and the flexible neck articulation allowed the animal to move directly above the seabed and feed close to the sediment.".

Researchers also believe the whale may have relied on its highly specialized echolocation system to locate prey beneath the soft sediment of coastal environments. Unlike other marine mammals that forage along the ocean floor, Scaphokogia lacked the sensitive facial whiskers or specialized visual adaptations that can help animals find food near the bottom.

Instead, its extraordinarily asymmetrical skull may have supported a sophisticated biological sonar system that allowed it to detect hidden prey.

This unusual feeding strategy represents a specialized way of life that no longer exists among modern marine mammals. As ocean conditions shifted toward the end of the Miocene, the ecological niche occupied by Scaphokogia disappeared, eventually giving way to the marine mammal communities familiar today.

The discovery provides a remarkable glimpse into how far evolution once pushed the anatomy of whales, producing a creature whose dramatically crooked face was not a deformity, but an adaptation to a vanished underwater world.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Listening to the in-game radio stations while you cruise around in Grand Theft Auto VI, you might hear a recruitment ad for the Vice City Police Department, which makes no secret of the kind of maladjusted psychos it's looking for.

According to recent reports, “Have you always dreamed of abusing your power without consequence?” one spot begins. “Well, now you can, when you join the Vice City Police Department, VCPD. You’ll have fun learning the ins and outs of applying excessive force.” The commercial goes on to suggest that cadets will be trained in racial profiling and planting evidence.

Industry observers note that given that blistering analysis of American law enforcement, you might imagine that actual cops aren’t massive fans of the latest GTA title, which was released after a 13-year wait on Thursday. Yet as millions of gamers have started to explore every stash house and back alley in the sun-drenched wilderness of a fictionalized South Florida, even police departments have attempted to exploit this monocultural mania to elevate their public messaging or recruit newly introduced officers.

It’s a curious strategy given that the series rewards theft and drug dealing while enticing you to run over pedestrians, but evidently the mere presence of law enforcement in the games (as the primary antagonists, mind you) was enough to inspire waves of AI slop celebrating the thin blue line.

An Instagram channel of the San Diego Police Department, for example, on Thursday posted an AI-generated image of an SDPD cruiser set against a sunset over the San Diego Bay. Its neon pinks and purples match the saturated aesthetic of GTA, and in case there was any doubt what the department was going for, the nonsensical phrase “Join San Diego PD VI” appears at the top. “Want to drive a police car, we can make that happen!” reads the caption. “Apply Now!”.

Another police department in Washington state shared GTA-like imagery on its Instagram page, encouraging viewers to try “the real-life version” of GTA VI by pursuing a career in law enforcement. “No cheat codes,” the caption advertised. “No respawns. Just real people, real challenges, and a career that makes a difference.” A wave of self-serious GTA slop also flooded the feeds of police departments in Canada, from Edmonton to Toronto—though the Calgary Police Service tried something more lighthearted by having one of their traffic officers react to clips of dangerous and illegal driving maneuvers in the game.

Among police departments that were not seeking to add to their ranks through GTA VI fever, many posted content aimed at reminding people that laws exist in real life. “Keep It In The Game VI,” advised a typical post on the Instagram account of the Glendale Police Department in California, complete with a GTA-fied police cruiser and view of the city. “Follow posted speed limits, respect the law, and keep your wanted level at ZERO!” the caption warned. The Denver Police Department, in similarly scolding fashion, informed followers: “Grand theft auto is still illegal.”.

The communications teams for these agencies should have perhaps reconsidered trying to farm engagement and clout from the massive success of GTA VI. As many commenters are noting, the game portrays cops as corrupt and quick to violence. Players have discovered that the Vice City squad will brutalize you if you start filming them during a questionable arrest. One clip highlighted a cop pulling his weapon on a character who had done nothing worse than stand in the street to take a selfie.

A certain dose of this authoritarian cruelty ought to appeal to the right-wing cranks upset that GTA VI is too “woke” when it comes to gender, race, and politics overall. It’s a little different when the most visible villains of the game are choosing to overlook its vicious take on their profession in order to spam epic social media posts.

Fox News, just for comparison, dutifully took the tired law-and-order line on GTA VI, with talking heads aghast at kids’ exposure to virtual gun violence (never mind actual gun deaths in the US) and an atmosphere of moral depravity. Elon Musk famously declared that he couldn’t play GTA games because they compelled you to shoot cops.

Both stances, however insincere, suggest a modicum of regard for law enforcement that the police departments themselves immediately jettisoned in favor of GTA cringe. They of course won’t win any cool points for it, but at least this way they can pretend to connect with the general population.

In a recent development, more baffling still is that the Russian army has generated its own GTA VI recruitment ads to blast out on its Telegram channel, and NATO has trumpeted its defensive security alliance with military-industrial GTA sludge, boasting that “even the best gamers would have a challenge” eluding fighter jets and submarines. Trying to parse Vice President JD Vance’s depiction of a Trumpian “golden age” with GTA graphics is a fool’s errand. In the most dystopian development of all, a US Army battalion in Georgia granted 43 eligible soldiers four days off to play the new GTA in return for reenlisting for another two years of service.

What do any of these institutions or their missions have to do with a video game where you rob convenience stores in flip-flops? Doesn’t matter. When the zeitgeist is this all-consuming, you fire up ChatGPT and find an angle, no matter how confusing. Surely someone, somewhere, will be tricked into thinking you have anything to do with it.

Mahershala Ali got candid about the impact — or lack thereof — his two Oscar wins have had on his career in Hollywood while appearing on a recent episode of Carmelo Anthony and Kazeem “Kaz” Famuyide’s “7PM in Brooklyn” podcast.

According to recent reports, the actor, who took home trophies for best supporting actor for both 2018’s “Greenbook” and 2016’s “Moonlight,” asked the hosts about the meaning of an Oscar, and if it really validates whether someone is “a good actor” or not. “There’s more good actors than there is good material,” he mentioned. “It’s not even that all these people are competing for these same spots. It’s just that out of all the material made, there’s only a handful of them that check certain boxes.” Related Stories Mel Gibson's 'The Resurrection of the Christ' Bought for Italy by RAI Cinema and Leone Film Group.

He continued: “The vast majority of projects that get greenlit, there are not roles for me in those. You gotta think that way, you know what I mean? So, it doesn’t matter if I got 17 Oscars. If someone is not writing something for you or greenlighting something with you in mind, you’re like everybody else waiting and looking and searching.”.

Industry observers note that while the star noted that actors could produce their own projects, the timeline is usually as least a “three to five year” journey. When asked by Famuyide if an Oscar win validates Black actors, Ali responded: “It’s kind of just talk. It doesn’t translate to anything real. You don’t want to find yourself in a situation where, oh, that’s ‘the diversity project.’ You just want to do great material as a Black person. You’re not thinking of yourself as this exotic other, per se. You just are living your life.”.

Most recently, Ali starred in Bassam Tariq’s “Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother,” which hit theaters on Sept. 25. Tariq was also the original director of Marvel’s failed “Blade” movie, in which Ali was set to star in the title role, which he recently discussed in an interview with The Latest Arab.

Industry observers note that “It was funny and strange to start casting and building without a proper script,” Tariq told interviewer Hanna Flint about his short-lived Marvel career. “You’re sitting there and explaining to actors what their role will be, and they just have to believe you. That’s also very dangerous because if the text comes and it doesn’t add up to what you were saying, your credibility gets completely shot. All I have is my integrity, and I’ve been thinking about that a lot.”.

In a recent development, “If you’re the bearer of bad news to your actors, but you’re not the one making any of these decisions — and it’s actually coming from a corporate entity — that’s not a great way to be a director,” he continued. “I know some people can take that and run with it, but I learned I was losing credibility with my actors, and it wasn’t a healthy way to operate as a filmmaker. Life’s too short to make shit films, so that was my massive lesson: I have to have full control over my script. If we disagree, it’s between them and me. It’s quite sad because we had such high hopes for what we wanted to build.”.

Industry observers note that speaking of the film’s inability to get made, Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige had previously said he felt “like a gigantic loser and failure,” a statement that Ali agreed with in a GQ interview in the months following. “To this day, I don’t know why it didn’t happen. I just know that it was—Kevin, he said it was the biggest failure of his career and I agree,” said Ali.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, A screenshot is how a lot of things get saved on a phone, from a dinner reservation to the address a friend just texted.
  • Signal, a nonprofit messaging app that uses end-to-end encryption to keep texts and calls private, is putting limits on what those assistants can see.
  • In a recent development, on iPhones running iOS 27, Signal's Block Siri AI setting is on by default.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A screenshot is how a lot of things get saved on a phone, from a dinner reservation to the address a friend just texted. AI assistants like Meta's Muse and Apple's Siri AI can now use what’s on the screen to answer questions or do things like add events to a calendar.

But not every platform is okay with that.

Signal, a nonprofit messaging app that uses end-to-end encryption to keep texts and calls private, is putting limits on what those assistants can see. On Friday, Nov. 20, the app revealed it will block screenshots on iPhones running iOS 27 and restrict AI screen capture on some Android devices.

In a recent development, on iPhones running iOS 27, Signal's Block Siri AI setting is on by default. On supported Android devices, Signal automatically turns on Screen security when it detects an assistant trying to read what's on the screen. People can turn either protection off in Signal's settings, though doing so could give an assistant with screen access a look at both sides of the conversation.

In a recent development, "Privacy is our mission; it’s why we exist, and we do everything we can to protect it," wrote Signal President Meredith Whittaker in Signal's blog post. The Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free right now with T-Mobile.

End-to-end encryption keeps a message private on its way from one person to another. When it arrives, the recipient's phone has to turn it back into words they can read. Those words might show up in the chat itself or in a notification.

According to recent reports, an AI assistant with access to either can read those messages, too. Once it has the text, Signal has no say in whether the assistant processes it on the phone or sends it to a remote server, according to their blog post.

Sources indicate that that can play out in surprisingly ordinary ways. Earlier this week, Reuters reported that a Meta employee got a reminder from the company’s Muse assistant to reply to her sister. The message was in Signal. "This seems like an extreme privacy violation. I definitely did not grant it access to other apps, or recall being asked about this," the employee wrote in an internal post.

Reuters worked with Signal and the AI Now Institute to see how that could happen using an Android phone and a Mac. They discovered that on the phone, Muse got the message text straight from a notification. On a Mac, it used accessibility tools and screenshots to read chats. In both tests, Muse relied on permissions granted during setup. Meta told Reuters that Muse can only access other apps through permissions customers explicitly grant.

Whittaker pointed to accessibility tools, which are designed to help people with disabilities use their devices. With broad permissions, she wrote, those tools can act as "a skeleton key that provides access to AI agents.".

She's thereby asking Apple, Google, and Microsoft to spell out what their assistants can read and give developers a way to block that access.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A century after the Taung Child transformed our understanding of where humans came from, scientists are discovering that this famous fossil still has surprises to reveal. A fresh study published in Nature dates the ancient remains to between 2.96 and 3.03 million years ago and suggests that the human family tree in southern Africa was much more complicated than previously believed.

Recent findings suggest that the international study was led by Professor Gabriele Macho of the Archaeology, Environmental Changes and Geo-Chemistry (AMGC) research group at Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB). The findings challenge long-standing assumptions about how early human relatives evolved and how different species were related.

According to recent reports, first discovered in South Africa in 1924, the Taung Child provided the first concrete evidence supporting the African origins of humanity. It also became the original "type specimen" used to define the species Australopithecus africanus. However, scientists never established definitive criteria for assigning later fossil discoveries to this species. As a result, the Taung Child remains the only fossil that can be identified with certainty as Australopithecus africanus.

"For over 100 years, we assumed the Taung Child was just one of many similar fossils from the era," states Professor Gabriele Macho. "Our findings turn that on its head. The human family tree wasn't a neat, straight trunk -- it was a chaotic, tangled bush driven by climate shifts.".

Ancient Fossils Reveal a More Complex Human Family Tree.

Recent findings suggest that to investigate how the Taung Child compared with other early human relatives, researchers examined tooth structure and patterns of brain and dental development during growth. They found that several adult fossils traditionally classified as Australopithecus africanus followed developmental patterns that differed from those of the Taung Child.

It has been revealed that differences in brain development were particularly revealing. They suggest that fossils previously grouped into a single species may actually represent several distinct hominin species that inhabited the Sterkfontein region, either at the same time or during different periods.

These findings raise key questions about the diversity of our ancient ancestors and suggest that early human evolution followed a much more complicated path than scientists once assumed.

How Climate Change Shaped Human Evolution.

According to recent reports, the researchers believe that dramatic environmental changes played a major role in creating this evolutionary diversity. Millions of years ago, southern Africa experienced repeated shifts between wetter and drier climates, continually transforming the landscape and the habitats available to early human relatives.

In a recent development, as suitable environments expanded and contracted, ancient hominin populations moved with them. Some groups became geographically isolated and evolved along different paths, while others eventually came back into contact and interbred. These changing conditions also exposed populations to different predators and pathogens, creating additional pressures that shaped their evolution.

According to recent reports, southern Africa's position along the boundary between tropical and temperate ecosystems made it especially important in this process. Over thousands of years, shifting habitats may have repeatedly brought different hominin species together, creating opportunities for interbreeding and hybridization.

A Greener South Africa 3 Million Years Ago.

The study also reveals a surprising picture of the environment in which the Taung Child lived. Evidence preserved in fossilized pollen indicates that the region was once considerably wetter and more heavily forested than it is today.

Researchers identified evidence of tree species that are now found hundreds of kilometers to the northeast, suggesting that the landscape surrounding the Taung Child was dramatically different from modern South Africa.

Together, these discoveries challenge the traditional view of human evolution as a relatively straightforward progression from one species to another. Instead, they point to a shifting network of populations that repeatedly separated, adapted, reunited, and sometimes interbred as environmental conditions changed.

More than 100 years after its discovery, the Taung Child is once again transforming our understanding of human origins. Its latest secrets suggest that the emergence of our own genus, Homo, was preceded by a far more diverse and interconnected world of ancient human relatives than previously recognized.

Russell Brand is selling merchandise calling for his freedom while he’s behind bars after being sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison after being found guilty of rape and sexual assault.

Recent findings suggest that it is unclear how long the items have been available for purchase on Reborn, however the earliest reviews on the varying products date to Nov. 16 (he was sentenced Nov. 9). “Prisoners are rightly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims,” Norris wrote on X. “This is being urgently investigated, and I expect action to be taken if he is found to have broken the rules.”.

Hims & Hers launches upcoming peptide treatments — while admitting there's more to learn about efficacy

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1578 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that hims & Hers Health on Wednesday said it will offer five formulations of peptides and longevity treatments compounded in the U.S.
  • Even as it announced the newly introduced products, Hims & Hers acknowledged it has more to learn about how best to use the peptides and how effective they are — underscoring the uncertainty surrounding the growing space.
  • The new offerings come after the federal government eased restrictions on compounding certain unapproved peptides, which are short chains of amino ​acids.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that hims & Hers Health on Wednesday said it will offer five formulations of peptides and longevity treatments compounded in the U.S. as part of the initial rollout of its Peptides+ platform, all of which are not approved by regulators.

Even as it announced the newly introduced products, Hims & Hers acknowledged it has more to learn about how best to use the peptides and how effective they are — underscoring the uncertainty surrounding the growing space.

The new offerings come after the federal government eased restrictions on compounding certain unapproved peptides, which are short chains of amino ​acids. Those products have exploded in popularity among fitness and longevity enthusiasts who attest that they help with muscle growth, rapid injury recovery and anti-aging, even though most lack evidence from robust human trials.

Hims in late October released an early access list for the upcoming peptide offerings, and more than 10,000 people signed up within 15 days, a company spokesperson mentioned in a statement.

None of the organization's specific compounded products are approved by the Food and Drug Administration. But Hims said they are authorized by law and formulated by pharmacies "that adhere to rigorous quality standards and are licensed and inspected by state boards of pharmacy.".

The products include compounded formulations of sermorelin, a peptide that stimulates growth-hormone release and is marketed for recovery, body composition and anti-aging; glutathione, a peptide promoted ‌for anti-aging and athletic recovery; and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, or NAD+, a coenzyme that plays a role in cellular metabolism.

The organization will also offer compounded versions of vitamin B-12, a vitamin needed to make red blood cells, build DNA, and maintain healthy nerve function, and L-carnitine, an amino acid derivative that helps the body turn fat into energy. The FDA has approved certain prescription forms of both peptides for established medical uses, primarily for diagnosed deficiencies in those compounds.

Sources indicate that hims noted it prepares to add more peptides and therapies made in the U.S. over time. That includes BPC-157, an unapproved peptide derived from a protein found in human gastric juice that is marketed for healing processes. The firm also aims to introduce another unapproved peptide called TB-500, which is derived from a naturally occurring protein in the body and is marketed for broader, systemic soft-tissue recovery and flexibility. Most of the research on both has been conducted in animals, not humans.

To receive the products, members on the Hims platform will start with an assessment of health history and goals with a licensed provider trained in peptide therapies, who can tailor a personalized strategy to their needs, if appropriate.

The manufacturer said it intends to use its communication platform to check in with patients and ensure they are seeing desired results.

"If they're not, we need to do something about it," Dr. Anant Vinjamoori, Hims chief medical officer, told CNBC. "We need to, you know, adjust the dose when that's appropriate, or in some cases consider other compounds that's maybe a better fit. And of course, there will also be cases when we need to refer people to other care options.".

However, Vinjamoori remarked there's still uncertainty over how to best use the peptides.

Industry observers note that "We don't have all of this data that we're used to having with compounds like this," he mentioned. "We have the opportunity to get it right, and I think we see that as our responsibility with a organization of our size, our skill, and resources to really lead.".

Vinjamoori added that people who have serious illnesses, such as cardiovascular disease, liver disease and kidney disease, will not be candidates for the compounds for now.

Meanwhile, Andrew Huberman, a well known neuroscientist, podcaster and Stanford University School of Medicine professor who recently joined Hims' board of directors, in a statement called compounds "real medical treatments, not just a wellness trend." He remarked Hims provides safe access through "trusted sourcing and physician oversight.".

Sources indicate that but health experts raised concerns about the broader mainstream marketing of peptides in the U.S. and accessing them on telehealth platforms.

Recent findings suggest that "With peptides, I think you have to view them the same way you would view any drug that hasn't been rigorously tested," said Joshua Kritzer, a chemistry professor at Tufts University. "Without actual testing, all you have is anecdotal information, and that's just not enough information to put a substance in your body.".

Kritzer noted the lack of large clinical trials means researchers can't rule out potentially serious, rare complications from peptides — the kinds of risks that have led regulators to reject or pull otherwise effective drugs from the market after they underwent comprehensive testing in humans.

It has been revealed that without that testing, it's also unclear how telehealth firms, physicians and pharmacies can make decisions about what doses patients should take, said Paul Knoepfler, a cell biology and human anatomy professor at UC Davis Health. While some people rely on anecdotal data from real peptide consumers, "the dosing for these products really has not been established," he added.

Knoepfler remarked one risk is that injecting too much of a synthetic peptide into patients could trigger "weird immune responses that are really bad for one's health" because the body might recognize it as foreign.

According to recent reports, "With the peptides, it's very loosey-goosey," Knoepfler told CNBC. "How does one even know what would be the effective amount for whatever you're hoping it will do, and what amount would have more risks?".

But he remarked the more contact patients can have with physicians around taking a compounded peptide, the better. Providers, including those tied to telehealth firms, should make sure patients are well-informed about the possible risks and unknowns of a given product and consider their preexisting conditions, cancer history and other medications, Knoepfler said.

Recent findings suggest that that appears to be consistent with the approach Hims & Hers is taking. The manufacturer says patients who use the peptide and longevity products can also use its Care+ offering, which pairs treatment with ongoing support. That includes twice-a-year lab testing to track their progress and the ability to message providers trained in peptide therapy around the clock with any questions.

Still, Kritzer argued that having a doctor who only knows a patient from online, essentially mail-order platforms or websites "is not enough supervision to put you on a prescription medication," especially an unapproved one.

According to recent reports, hims' ability to legally sell some of these peptides stems from a major shift in federal oversight by the Health and Human Services Department. It issued a policy in October that says the Food and Drug Administration will not take enforcement action against licensed pharmacies, federal facilities or physicians that compound and dispense six unapproved peptides while formal rules are reviewed.

According to recent reports, in practice, that means these pharmacies and other firms can now offer them, even though the peptides aren't yet on the FDA's official list of ingredients compounding pharmacies are allowed to make. It does not translate to formal approval of the specific peptides.

The policy followed a 2023 decision by the Biden administration where the FDA restricted compounding pharmacies from producing popular peptide formulations due to safety, impurity and immune-reaction concerns.

HHS Secretary ​Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has supported broader access to peptides, calling himself a "big fan" of the treatments and arguing that restrictions were driving Americans to potentially unsafe products from overseas. Kennedy has previously described using BPC-157 to treat a muscle injury.

The announcement also comes after Hims in February 2025 acquired a California-based peptide manufacturing facility equipped with advanced peptide synthesizers.

The evidence for peptide efficacy varies by compound.

A 2026 systematic review screening 113 studies, including both small trials on humans along with rodent research, found zero eligible clinical outcome trials proving that administering IV or intramuscular NAD+ improves anti-aging, energy, or wellness endpoints in humans.

Sources indicate that there is some evidence for specific uses of certain peptides, such as potential weight loss. A review of 37 L-carnitine trials found participants lost about 2.7 pounds on average, though that analysis does not demonstrate that a compounded injection works the same way.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, vitamin B-12 injections are most commonly used to help people with a diagnosed deficiency rather than preventative care. U.S. survey data indicates only 3.6% of adults are B-12 deficient.

It has been revealed that glutathione's evidence is thin, too. IV injections of it are widely marketed for skin whitening, yet not FDA-approved for this purpose.

A small study published in the Journal of Pakistan Association of Dermatologists evaluating IV glutathione showed that the treatment is "not very effective" for skin-lightening, and that it loses efficacy with time.

The FDA also stated in August that it received reports of at least 30 patients who experienced adverse events after they received compounded IV glutathione alone or in combination with other ingredients from different compounding pharmacies.

All of the glutathione tied to the reports were from the same wholesale distributor and was labeled as dietary supplement grade, which is not an appropriate ingredient to make injectable drugs. Two of the Texas pharmacies conducted recalls related to elevated endotoxin levels in their glutathione injectable drugs.

These studies and reports don't speak to how Hims' exact combination will perform, but they do highlight the current limits on data studying the treatments and the questions surrounding them.

European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth.
  • The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov.
  • Recent findings suggest that the significant moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth.

The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet.

Recent findings suggest that the significant moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes.

BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio.

The duo debuted — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018, beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system.

Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun. Spacecraft approaching the solar system's innermost planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug.

Recent findings suggest that so the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth, two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year, however, after the mission suffered an concern with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters.

Today's orbital insertion is the latest milestone in BepiColombo's Mercury arrival phase, which is expected to take about six months in total.

According to recent reports, arrival began on Sept. 3, when the MTM released MPO and Mio. The two orbiters remain connected today; they won't separate until Dec. 9 or thereabouts.

It has been revealed that shortly thereafter, Mio will settle into its final orbit, a highly elliptical path that will take it over Mercury's poles. MPO is also destined for a polar orbit, though a much less elliptical one than Mio's; the ESA probe will conduct a series of engine burns before finally getting there on March 10, 2027.

BepiColombo won't start doing science work until April 6, 2027. The two probes will gather complementary data from their two different vantage points, shedding a great deal of light on a mysterious world.

"The mission will study all aspects of Mercury, from the structure and dynamics of its magnetosphere and how it interacts with the solar wind, to its internal structure with its large iron core, and the origin of the planet’s magnetic field," ESA officials wrote in a BepiColombo mission description.

"The data will enable scientists to understand more about the origin and evolution of a planet located close to its parent star, and a better understanding of the overall evolution of our solar system," they added.

Michael Wall is the Spaceflight and Tech Editor for Space.com and joined the team in 2010. He primarily covers human and robotic spaceflight, military space, and exoplanets, but has been known to dabble in the space art beat. His book about the search for alien life, "Out There," was published on Nov. 13, 2018. Before becoming a science writer, Michael worked as a herpetologist and wildlife biologist. He has a Ph.D. in evolutionary biology from the University of Sydney, Australia, a bachelor's degree from the University of Arizona, and a graduate certificate in science writing from the University of California, Santa Cruz. Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on November 21, 2026

💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you look up at the sky tonight, you'll notice the Moon is looking noticeably fuller than it did earlier in the week.
  • According to recent reports, as of Saturday, Nov.
  • Sources indicate that if you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Imbrium and Vaporum, as well as the Kepler Crater.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you look up at the sky tonight, you'll notice the Moon is looking noticeably fuller than it did earlier in the week. We're still in the Waxing Gibbous phase, which falls between the First Quarter and Full Moon, but we're getting closer to the Full Moon every night.

According to recent reports, as of Saturday, Nov. 21, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waxing Gibbous phase, with 85% of its surface visible.

Sources indicate that if you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Imbrium and Vaporum, as well as the Kepler Crater. With binoculars, you'll also see the Mare Frigoris, the Clavius Crater, and the Mare Nectaris. And if you have a telescope, you'll get to see all this plus the Apollo 15 and 17 landing spots, and the Rima Hyginus.

The next Full Moon will take place on November 24.

According to NASA, the Moon goes through a complete cycle of phases roughly every 29.5 days. As it orbits Earth, the portion of its sunlit surface visible to us changes, giving rise to the different lunar phases. The cycle begins with a New Moon, progresses to a Full Moon, and then gradually returns to a New Moon before starting all over again.

Fresh Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye).

Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere).

In a recent development, first Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon.

Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet.

Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible.

According to recent reports, waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere).

Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit.

Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.

Scientists tested 212 plant-based foods. Every single one contained fungal toxins

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1086 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every one of 212 plant-based foods and drinks tested in a latest study contained at least one naturally occurring fungal toxin, raising questions about the potential health effects of regularly consuming these products.
  • Recent findings suggest that researchers examined a wide selection of vegetarian and vegan products sold in the UK, including meat alternatives and dairy substitutes.
  • It has been revealed that mycotoxins are poisonous substances produced by certain fungi, including molds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every one of 212 plant-based foods and drinks tested in a latest study contained at least one naturally occurring fungal toxin, raising questions about the potential health effects of regularly consuming these products.

Recent findings suggest that researchers examined a wide selection of vegetarian and vegan products sold in the UK, including meat alternatives and dairy substitutes. They detected at least one of 19 mycotoxins in every product, and many contained multiple toxins.

It has been revealed that mycotoxins are poisonous substances produced by certain fungi, including molds. They can enter the food supply when agricultural crops become contaminated during growing, harvesting, or storage.

Recent findings suggest that the investigation was led by scientists at the University of Parma in Italy, with contributions from Cranfield University. The researchers analyzed 212 products, including plant-based meat alternatives (PMBAs) and plant-based beverages (PBBs). The selection covered foods commonly found on supermarket shelves, such as vegan burgers, vegetarian chicken pieces, vegan sausages, and oat, almond, and soy milk.

Although the findings highlight how widespread these naturally occurring contaminants can be, the researchers also identified an important reassuring detail. Every product contained mycotoxin concentrations below recommended European Union guideline levels, which the team said reflected the high food quality standards maintained by the UK food industry.

Why Plant-Based Foods Can Contain Fungal Toxins.

Many of the ingredients used to manufacture plant-based foods are particularly susceptible to fungal contamination. Grains, legumes, and seeds can encounter mold in fields or storage facilities, creating opportunities for mycotoxins to develop before the ingredients reach food manufacturers.

It has been revealed that unlike bacteria or viruses, mycotoxins are chemical substances produced by certain fungi. Their presence in food does not necessarily mean the product contains living mold, and detecting a toxin does not automatically mean the food is unsafe. The potential health risk depends on factors such as the type of toxin, its concentration, and how much a person consumes over time.

It has been revealed that this distinction is especially important for people who eat plant-based products frequently. Someone whose diet regularly includes meat substitutes, dairy alternatives, grains, and legumes may encounter these substances through several different foods rather than a single source.

Could Repeated Exposure Pose Health Risks?

While the concentrations detected in the UK products were below recommended EU guidelines, researchers say the potential effects of repeated exposure deserve closer attention.

Earlier studies have suggested that consuming small amounts of mycotoxins regularly may contribute to cumulative exposure and potentially increase health risks. In other words, assessing a single product may not provide a complete picture of a person's overall dietary exposure.

Eating one of these products occasionally is unlikely to cause problems based on the levels reported. However, a diet that relies heavily or exclusively on plant-based foods could involve repeated exposure to mycotoxins from numerous ingredients and products. Researchers say understanding the combined effects is important for evaluating possible long-term health consequences.

The severity of mycotoxin exposure varies depending on the compounds involved and the amount consumed. At sufficiently high or harmful exposure levels, certain mycotoxins can damage the liver and kidneys, interfere with normal immune system function, and increase the risk of cancer.

Recent findings suggest that the new findings do not establish that the tested products cause these conditions. Instead, they provide information that scientists can use to estimate how much exposure consumers may receive through their diets and develop more accurate food safety risk assessments for the UK population.

Scientists Call for Better Monitoring of Plant-Based Ingredients.

Sources indicate that andrea Patriarca, Senior Lecturer in Mycology at Cranfield University, emphasized that mycotoxins are a natural part of the food environment and should not discourage people from eating a varied diet. Mycology is the branch of biology devoted to studying fungi, including molds and yeasts.

"Mycotoxins occur naturally in foods and cannot be completely avoided. As consumers, we should not be frightened or deterred from enjoying a variety of products.

However, a significant concern arises when latest foods enter the market, as there are currently no established regulations to monitor mycotoxins. We collaborate closely with various sectors in the food industry, from farmers to food companies, to help implement effective mycotoxin management integrated within food safety standards. The data from our research helps food safety organizations in assessing risks, particularly in complex multi-ingredient products.

Industry observers note that we are right now collaborating with the University of Parma to evaluate the risks faced by the population based on different dietary habits. Our aim is to advise policymakers and raise awareness among vulnerable consumers.".

Sources indicate that the researchers are particularly interested in how food safety monitoring can keep pace with the growing range of plant-based products. Foods made from multiple ingredients present additional challenges because each component may introduce different contaminants, making overall exposure more difficult to assess.

In a recent development, their work also underscores the importance of monitoring raw materials throughout the food production process. Identifying and controlling contamination before ingredients are combined into finished products could help manufacturers manage potential risks more effectively.

What the Findings Mean for Plant-Based Diets.

The discovery of fungal toxins in all 212 products highlights the importance of studying dietary exposure across multiple foods, rather than evaluating each product in isolation.

Industry observers note that for consumers, the results are not a reason to abandon vegan or vegetarian foods. The concentrations measured were below recommended EU guidelines, and the researchers stress that mycotoxins cannot be completely eliminated from the food supply.

Instead, the study points to the need for continued research into how different eating habits influence exposure, particularly among people who depend heavily on plant-based products. The University of Parma and Cranfield University are continuing their collaboration to investigate these dietary patterns, identify potentially vulnerable groups, and provide evidence that can inform future food safety policies.

The research, titled "Mycotoxin contamination in plant-based beverages and meat alternatives: A survey of the UK market," was published in the journal Food Control.

The study was conducted as part of the European Union-funded Horizon Europe FunShield4Med project (HORIZON-WIDERA-2021-ACCESS-03), Grant Agreement No 101079173.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany, who finished top of Group A2 following their 5-0 win over the Netherlands in Berlin on Monday are to face Belgium in the Nations League quarterfinals — after they finished second in Group A1. The Belgians recently came up with a statement result of their own, beating Italy 4-1. The match-up between the neighboring countries promises to be closely contested, with Belgium sitting at No. 8 in the men's rankings, three places above Germany.

The head coach of Belgium is former Bayern Munich player Mark van Bommel, who took over from Rudi Garcia following the World Cup, where they were knocked out by eventual champions Spain in the quarterfinals.

Germany head into the knockout phase on a high note, not only because they won their group, but also the way they performed in their last two matches, against Serbia and the Netherlands in the group stage.

In a recent development, germany head coach Jürgen Klopp followed the draw, held in Nyon on Friday, from the German FA's (DFB) Frankfurt offices. He played down the notion that Germany enter the tie as the favorites.

"I've practically never given it any thought. It's never interested me," he said.

According to recent reports, "An awful lot can happen in that time. We're very happy with the final impression we left, yet we're also fully aware that we're only at the very beginning of a development process. We want to carry this positive momentum forward—there's still a great deal to be done.".

The matches are slated for March 25 and March 30, 2027, and having won their group, Germany will have home-field advantage for the second leg.

Germany and Belgium have faced each other 26 times to date, with West Germany and Germany having the upper hand with 20 wins, five defeats and one draw.

Should Germany advance to the semifinals, they will go on to face the winner of England and Norway, a World Cup quarterfinals rematch.

In the other two semifinals matchups, the Netherlands drew Portugal, while the top pairing sees Spain face France in a rematch of one of last summer's World Cup semifinals.

The "Final Four" mini tournament is to be held from June 9 to 13 but the host venue won't be determined until the semifinal lineup has been completed.
